models.title: Geometrically linked time-weighted return
models.summary: Two-sub-period TWR as the compounded product of relative sub-period returns minus one.

relationship.original_equation: r_twr = (1 + r_t,1) x (1 + r_t,2) - 1 (Eq2, two-sub-period form)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM3 geometric linking Eq2 with Exhibits 2-4, printed pp. 152-155 (PDF pp. 160-163): Ex2 true TWR (1-0.01)x(1+0.0142)-1 = 0.41%; Ex3/Ex4 true TWRs 8.00%; practice Q4 solutions, printed p. 187 (PDF p. 195): February 6.76%, March 4.80%, Q1 16.36%
relationship.translation_notes: Fixed two-sub-period form (the PDF's Eq2 generalizes to n sub-periods; three-period Q1 total 16.36% is cited as supporting evidence). Decimals.

variables.definition: TWR of the first sub-period, decimal
TWR of the second sub-period, decimal
Geometrically linked TWR for the full period, decimal

assumptions: Sub-period returns from intra-period valuation at each large cash flow; GIPS requires geometric (multiplicative) linking.
limitations: Two-sub-period closed form only; three or more sub-periods extend the product (Q1: 16.36% over Jan/Feb/Mar). Returns compound, never add.

models.title: Modified Dietz estimated return
models.summary: Day-weighted cash-flow approximation of TWR: net gain over beginning value plus day-weighted net flows.

relationship.original_equation: r_ModDietz = (V1 - V0 - CF)/(V0 + sum CF_i x w_i) (Eq3, single-flow form)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM3 Modified Dietz Eq3 and day-weight Eq4 with Exhibits 2-3, printed pp. 153-155 (PDF pp. 161-163): w = (30-5)/30 = 0.83; Ex2-left (110,550-100,000-10,000)/(100,000+10,000x0.83) = 0.51%; Ex3-left 7.93%, Ex3-right 7.99%
relationship.translation_notes: Single-net-flow closed form (CF = sum of signed flows; w = day weight from Eq4). Decimals. Multi-flow sums extend the denominator additively.

variables.definition: Ending portfolio value, in currency units
Beginning portfolio value, in currency units
Net external cash flow (signed), in currency units
Day-weight of the flow (proportion of period held), decimal

assumptions: No valuation at the flow date (else use true TWR); flows assumed end-of-day per PDF note.
limitations: Estimate, not true TWR (10 bp gap in the worked example: 0.51% vs 0.41%); accuracy degrades with large flows in volatile markets (Exhibits 2-4).

models.title: Asset-weighted composite return
models.summary: Composite return as the sum of portfolio return-times-weight products; family holds precomputed products.

relationship.original_equation: r_C = sum r_pi x (V_0,pi/sum V_0,pi) (Eq7); alternate weights V_pi/sum V_pi (Eq8)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM3 composite asset-weighting Eqs 7-8 with Exhibits 5-6, printed pp. 159-162 (PDF pp. 167-170): beginning-assets method 0.0051x0.23+0.0028x0.224+0.0032x0.2597+0.0136x0.2863 = 0.65%; plus-weighted-cash-flows method = 0.62%; aggregate Dietz 0.62%
relationship.translation_notes: Family R holds precomputed r_pi x w_pi products (multiplication documented here as the per-element construction). Decimals. Eq7 (beginning assets) and Eq8 (plus weighted cash flows) share this form with different weights.

variables.source_symbol: r_pi x w_pi per portfolio (introduced family of products)
variables.definition: Portfolio return times its composite weight, decimal

assumptions: Weights from one consistent method (Eq7 or Eq8) summing to 100%; portfolio returns contemporaneous.
limitations: Weighting frequency matters: less-frequent asset-weighting misstates aggregate performance (PDF note). Arithmetic shared with portfolio-of-sectors sums; distinct GIPS equation and oracles (see gaps).
